_comment: Card 1 — quality_tier A (0.95) · high confidence RECOMMENDATION · Product-tier data · policy passed · 15% discount
diagnosis_summary: Customer C0042 is 50% overdue for replenishment of product P1011 (overdue_ratio=1.50, cycle measured at Product tier). This customer is overdue for replenishment of a product they have historically purchased on a regular cycle. The delay exceeds the product's historical interpurchase average by 20% or more, inventory is available, and a discount offer is commercially viable given current margin levels. The most likely cause is passive churn risk rather than active dissatisfaction.

evidence_chain.observation: Customer has not repurchased a previously bought product within its expected replenishment window (overdue_ratio >= 1.2).
evidence_chain.implication: The customer is at risk of churning from this SKU, whether due to competitive substitution, satisfaction issues, or simply forgetting.

evidence_chain.observation: Overdue ratio exceeds 1.2x the product-level median interpurchase gap, derived from >= 5 historical purchase gaps (falling back to aisle-level or department-level median if product data is sparse).
evidence_chain.implication: The delay is material (>20% over expected cycle), not noise. The interpurchase cycle estimate is robust enough to act on.

evidence_chain.observation: Inventory is above the fulfillment floor (mock_inventory > 50 units).
evidence_chain.implication: The SKU can be offered with confidence. Suppressing offers for out-of-stock items avoids bad customer experience and wasted send.

evidence_chain.observation: Post-discount gross margin remains above the margin floor (>= 15%) after applying the discount capped at 15%.
evidence_chain.implication: The action is commercially viable. The discount does not erode contribution margin below the minimum acceptable threshold.

likely_causes.cause: Customer passively deprioritized or forgot to repurchase
likely_causes.supporting_evidence: Overdue ratio between 1.2 and 1.8 with no prior complaint or return signal. The most common cause of mild overdue ratios.

likely_causes.cause: Customer is trialing a competing product
likely_causes.supporting_evidence: No direct signal available. Inferred when overdue ratio exceeds 2.0 and the customer has a history of multi-brand exploration (low F score).

likely_causes.cause: Customer experienced a negative product or delivery experience
likely_causes.supporting_evidence: No complaint or return signal available in this dataset. Should be cross-checked against customer service data if available.

checks_to_run.description: Confirm the customer's RFM segment before acting.
checks_to_run.why: Discount offers should be prioritized for High-Value or Loyal segments to protect margin. Lower-value segments (New, Lapsed) should receive lighter-touch interventions.
checks_to_run.confirm_if: rfm_segment is one of [High-Value, Loyal, At-Risk, Champions]

checks_to_run.description: Confirm overdue ratio magnitude to calibrate intervention type.
checks_to_run.why: A ratio of 1.2 warrants a light nudge; a ratio > 2.5 may indicate true churn where a discount alone will not recover the customer.

checks_to_run.description: Verify post-discount gross margin remains above 15%.
checks_to_run.why: Offering a discount that erodes margin below the floor is commercially harmful and violates the policy engine's hard constraint.

recommendations.recommendation: Offer a 15% discount on the overdue product. All policy constraints passed (margin and inventory floors met).
If margin or inventory constraints block a discount, send a no-offer reminder message to keep the brand and product top-of-mind without a commercial incentive.

do_not_recommend.reason: Suppressing the product listing would eliminate organic repurchase opportunity and is entirely disproportionate to a replenishment delay signal.
A refund offer is not warranted by a replenishment delay alone. It would signal product failure and set a harmful commercial precedent.

why: Re-engaging an at-risk replenishment customer is expected to recover one purchase cycle and reduce per-SKU churn probability within the 30-day window following the send.

why_not.reason: Suppressing the product listing would eliminate organic repurchase opportunity and is entirely disproportionate to a replenishment delay signal.
A refund offer is not warranted by a replenishment delay alone. It would signal product failure and set a harmful commercial precedent.

expected_impact_proxy.description: Re-engaging an at-risk replenishment customer is expected to recover one purchase cycle and reduce per-SKU churn probability within the 30-day window following the send.
expected_impact_proxy.estimated_improvement: Historical CPG benchmarks: replenishment nudges recover 15-30% of at-risk customers within one cycle window when the customer is in a High-Value or Loyal segment.
